items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to authorizing the
town of Hempstead in the county of Nassau to establish residential parking
systems in the neighborhoods of Bellerose Terrace and Elmont
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7554

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to authorizing
the town of Hempstead in the county of Nassau to establish residential
parking systems in the neighborhoods of Bellerose Terrace and Elmont

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill relates to authorizing the town of Hempstead in the county of
Nassau to establish a residential parking system in the neighborhoods of
Bellerose Terrace and Elmont.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends the vehicle and traffic law to authorize
the town of Hempstead to adopt a residential parking permit system.

Section two of the bill states that Notwithstanding the provisions of
any law to the contrary, the board of trustees of the town of Hempstead
may, by adoption of a local law or ordinance, provide for a residential
parking permit system and fix and require the payment of the fees appli-
cable to parking within the area in which such parking system is in
effect in accordance with the provisions of this section.

Section three of the bill provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

As a result of the redevelopment of the Belmont Park Racetrack, resi-
dents who abide adjacent to the development site will be burdened with
an influx of consumers and fans in their neighborhoods. The lack of
parking for residents of certain areas of the town of Hempstead, Nassau
county, has resulted in traffic hazards, congestion and air and noise
pollution. In addition, such lack of parking poses a hazard to residents
and other pedestrians in such areas. As such, a residential parking
system would be in the public interest while reducing such hazards and
pollution levels as well.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

No fiscal impact.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

The lack of parking for residents of certain areas of the town of Hemp-

air and noise pollution. In addition, such lack of parking poses a
hazard to residents and other pedestrians in such areas. As such, a
residential parking system would be in the public interest while reduc-
ing such hazards and pollution levels as well.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:
